angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 60,157,875 km at 60.53 pc = 13.29 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: distance 60.533 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.034), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 60.533 +/- 2.058 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 86.471 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: radius 86.471 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1403.71 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.074) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 60,157,875 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3802 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: effective temperature 3802 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.048) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: effective temperature 3802 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.048) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 6860 (pscomppars): spectral type M0 III, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 6860 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.03 dex, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 6860 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 3.22398, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 6860 (pscomppars): rotation period 7900 d, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 6860 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 6 km/s, from Lee et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...678A.106L/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.05 from 2020AJ....160..120J; the 11 published values span log g 1 to 1.6, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..120J)
